summary.text: 看 is traditionally analyzed as a hand above an eye, shading it to gaze into the distance. This received interpretation is not confirmed by a securely dated early inscription.

formation.text: A semantic compound in the received Shuowen analysis: 手 and 目 combine in the image of a hand shading the eyes while gazing. The account describes the construction but does not confirm it from a securely dated early form.

components.text: 手 depicts the hand above 目 in the traditional gaze-shading interpretation.
目 depicts the eye below 手 in the traditional interpretation.

history.text: The received Shuowen analysis places 手 above 目 and records an alternate graph, 𥉏, written with 倝 as a phonetic. The alternate’s date and graphic relationship to 看 are unresolved; no sequence of graphic change or corruption between the forms is established.

uncertainties.text: The hand-shading interpretation is not confirmed by a securely dated early inscription. The earliest written attestation of 看 and the date of 𥉏 remain unresolved.

senses.gloss: gaze or look into the distance
senses.text: The received Shuowen gloss 睎也 is explained in later commentary as shading the eyes with the hand to gaze. This is the earliest sense supported by the cited account, though the earliest historical occurrence of the spoken word is unresolved.
Looking, seeing, and observing are recorded meanings. Their relationship to the gaze gloss and to one another is not dated here.

senses.period: transmitted early medieval text examples; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: A transmitted early medieval text gives an example of watching or keeping observation. The evidence neither dates the origin of this use nor connects it sequentially to “gaze.”

senses.period: transmitted early medieval text example; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: A transmitted early medieval text gives an example glossed “visit.” The evidence does not show whether or how this use developed from “look.”

senses.period: later literary examples; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Dictionary and later literary examples record these uses. The evidence does not establish a dated semantic chain linking them to the gaze or look senses.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a chronology or semantic pathway among the recorded meanings; dictionary examples are not a complete dated corpus history.

Two historical readings are reported, and both have been glossed “see” in older lexicographic tradition. This does not show that the modern “look” and “guard” senses arose as a chronological split by pronunciation.

overview.text: 看 is traditionally explained as a hand above an eye, shading it to gaze into the distance. The received interpretation is not confirmed by a securely dated early inscription.

components.text: 手 is the hand above the eye in the traditional gaze-shading interpretation.
目 is the eye beneath the hand in that interpretation.

takeaway.text: The received account explains the gaze meaning, but the evidence does not connect it in a dated sequence to uses such as “guard” or “visit.”

relationships.text: In the received Shuowen analysis, 手 depicts the hand above 目 in the gaze-shading interpretation.
In the received Shuowen analysis, 目 depicts the eye below 手 in the gaze-shading interpretation.
